These Appeals Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

MFA No.201144/2018 is filed by the Insurance Company being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 15.03.2018 passed in MVC No.146/2016 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and MACT,
Chittapur (for short 'Tribunal'), by which the Tribunal while partly allowing the claim petition has granted compensation of Rs.6,14,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation to the claimant and has directed respondent No.2 - Insurance Company to deposit the same.
MFA No.201082/2018 is filed by the claimant, seeking enhancement of compensation.

The accident in question that occurred on 08.07.2015 involving Hero Splendor Plus motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-32/EC-1741 which was insured with the Reliance General Insurance Company causing accident resulting in injuries to the claimant is not in dispute.
The Tribunal, taking into consideration the material evidence produced has awarded compensation of Rs.6,14,000/- as noted above.
Aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company is before this Court, while the claimant is seeking enhancement of the same.

3. Sri Subhash Mallapur, learned counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company in MFA No.201144/2018 submits that the Tribunal has taken the income of the claimant at Rs.9,000/- per month without any basis and similarly has assessed the disability of the claimant at 21.66%, though the Doctor who has been examined as PW.2 has not treated the claimant.

He submits that the claimant himself was negligent in causing the accident and NC: 2023:KHC-K:8563 these aspects of the matters are not taken note of by the Tribunal while granting exorbitant compensation.

4. On the other hand, Sri Sanjeev Patil, learned counsel appearing for the appellant/claimant in MFA No.201082/2018 submits that the claimant was carrying on centering work and was earning handsome income from the said work.

That, the accident was caused while he was walking and there Mativanth vs Jagadish And Anr on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98956947/
3 cannot be any issue of negligence on his part.
He submits that the Tribunal ought to have taken into consideration the skill of the claimant with regard to the nature of work being carried on by him.
He submits that assessment of income at Rs.9,000/- per month is on lower side.

He further submits that due to the accident, the claimant suffered sclerosis of distal part of talus suggestive of old fracture of talus with internal fixation pin seen in situ in distal part of talus and proximal part of navicilar bone.

He submits that considering the nature of injuries suffered and the deposition of PW.2 assessing the disability at 65%, the Tribunal has NC: 2023:KHC-K:8563 erroneously taken the same at Rs.21.66% without any basis.
Thus, he submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on a lower side and the same requires to be enhanced.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
6.
The accident is of the year 2015.
As per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the notional income in respect of the victims of the road traffic accident for the year 2015 is Rs.8,000/- per month.
Since no documents have been produced by the claimant, in normal circumstances, notional income fixed in the said chart would have been taken into consideration.

However, since the claimant claims to have had skill in carrying the centering work, the assessment of income at Rs.9,000/- per month by the Tribunal is justified and same does not call for any interference.
There is no evidence placed on record with regard to disability resulting in reduction of his earning capacity.
However, the Tribunal in the facts and circumstances of the case has assessed the disability at 21.66% which is 1/3rd of the disability assessed by PW.2.
The same also cannot be found fault with and is thus maintained as it is.
The compensation awarded on other heads also appears to be just and proper.
8. In that view of the matter, no grounds are made out either by the Insurance Company questioning grant of quantum of compensation or by the claimant seeking enhancement.
Accordingly, both the appeals are dismissed.
The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is confirmed.
The amount in deposit, if any, is ordered to be transmitted to the Tribunal.
